title: Targets, pointing, touch, and motor effort
outcome: Design controls that are easy to reach and distinguish, beyond making icons larger.
useCase: Dense toolbars, table actions, and mobile operational screens.
benefits: Reduces avoidable motor errors and missed controls.
drawbacks: Space is limited; target design must balance density and task needs.
version: Web UX · WCAG 2.2 · principles, not magic formulas
cue: Make the intended action easy to hit and hard to confuse.

trace.title: Intended action
trace.detail: Fitts’s law connects pointing movement difficulty with target distance and size in a given task. The practical cue is useful: tiny distant targets are often harder to acquire. It does not mean every primary button should fill the entire screen.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Point at the intended target → move → acquire it → confirm the outcome. Watch misclicks and corrective movement. Then complete the same task with keyboard focus and a narrow touch screen.

When a target moves after the user starts pointing because an image loads above it, size alone will not fix the error. Stable layout is part of target reliability.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A large icon inside a tiny clickable wrapper can still have a small target. A tooltip-only accessible name can be absent for keyboard or touch users.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Design controls that are easy to reach and distinguish, beyond making icons larger. Explain one example and one failure.
